Wrong P and reversed ordered terminals fail deck; wrong unused top pin is missed by deck simplify but caught by explicit exact census.

actual_new_findings.finding: Wrong tap perimeter and reversed ordered terminals are rejected by the native deck; extracted layout tap parameters are unchanged in both cases.

The default simplify phase removes an unused renamed schematic top port. The strict deck flag alone then returns success with three schematic ports versus four layout ports. The new wrapper retains that raw verdict and rejects it using the exact top-port census; this is a concrete verifier gap, not an I/O parameter fix.

Moving only the seven native well/substrate markers to the parent preserves all 21 flattened layer masks (XOR=0), all non-marker cell-local shapes/contacts and every instance. Both taps disappear and native LVS fails. This confirms the known cell-local extraction limitation; device disappearance never counts as a repair.

authoritative_observations.finding: The published independent deep-tap fixture passes the unchanged pinned 53-file deck with tap extraction enabled, strict port flag and independent exact top-port census. Native literal ptap A/P=21.276/141.84 and ntap=24.06/160.4 match the original upstream CDL; these are non-square parameters.

The pinned reader already prioritizes explicit A and P/Perim with correct units. CustomTap preserves ordered terminals and enables A/P. The combiner sums A and P only for same ordered terminal nets. The fixture independently exercises that literal interpretation; it does not endorse a square normalization or R-only comparison.

Public PCell source generates rectangular active from its input W/L, and the generic symbol derives A/P accordingly. Existing original I/O CDL has 64 square W=L metadata rows with matching published R to printed precision. No arithmetic, unit or alias bug is demonstrated in generation or reading; the independent intended W/L or arbitrary-shape contract of those I/O instances is absent.
The simulation tap subcircuits consume only R; W/L are retained but unused. Changing LVS A/P alone would not update or validate the original electrical substrate resistance model.
The I/O library contributor describes arbitrary-shape and hierarchy-overlap ambiguity, not replacement numeric A/P values or a qualified general contract.

The pinned I/O library publishes CDL/doc/GDS/LEF/Liberty/SPICE/Verilog views. Its current public directory inventory does not supply the original editable I/O schematic/CDF parameter-generation history. This inventory is not a claim about unavailable private upstream source.

correction_decision.demonstrable_error: The existing protected physical contact role cannot realize literal P87.9um under the witnessed enclosure branch (conditional bound140.4um). This establishes inconsistency of the pair, but not which independently intended library representation should replace it.
correction_decision.not_demonstrated: No source-level formula, scaling, Perim alias or serialization defect explains the original I/O square parameters. The public non-square fixture does not supply intended parameter values for those different I/O masters.
required_independent_data: Original I/O schematic/CDF generation inputs or an upstream intended geometry/model specification naming each tap and its contact ownership, including parent overlap/merging.
A coherent reference and electrical model for the same geometry, including resistance or qualified substrate RC behavior; copying measured extraction into expected CDL would not supply this.
Corrected consistent library views with strict isolated and actual-parent validation, retaining devices/contacts/ports and physical qualification obligations.
